questions.question: Which organisation was founded by Raja Ram Mohan Roy in 1828?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Brahmo Samaj**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Raja Ram Mohan Roy**, widely regarded as the **'Father of Modern India'** and the pioneer of the **Indian Renaissance**, founded the **Brahmo Sabha** on **20th August 1828** in **Calcutta**.
 
• The organization was later renamed the **Brahmo Samaj** and functioned as a socio-religious reform movement aimed at purging Hindu society of **superstitions** and **dogmas**.
 
• The **Brahmo Samaj** advocated for **monotheism**, the worship of one formless God, and strongly opposed **idol worship**, **polytheism**, and **animal sacrifice**.
 
• It played a monumental role in the abolition of the **Sati system** in **1829**, through Roy's persistent advocacy and collaboration with **Lord William Bentinck**.
 
• The movement emphasized the rational interpretation of the **Vedas** and the **Upanishads**, promoting a synthesis of **Western rationalism** and **Eastern spirituality**.
 
• Roy's efforts through the Samaj also focused on **women's rights**, including the promotion of **widow remarriage** and access to **modern education**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Ramakrishna Mission**:

 
 
• Founded by **Swami Vivekananda** in **1897** at **Belur Math** near **Kolkata**.
 
• It is named after his guru, **Ramakrishna Paramhansa**, and focuses on **humanitarian relief** and **social service** as a form of worship.
 
 
 
• **Prarthana Samaj**:
 
 
• Established by **Atmaram Pandurang** in **1867** in **Bombay**.
 
• It was influenced by the **Brahmo Samaj** and led by prominent figures like **Mahadev Govind Ranade**, focusing on **caste reform** and **education for women**.
 
 
 
• **Arya Samaj**:
 
 
• Founded by **Swami Dayanand Saraswati** in **1875** in **Bombay**.
 
• The movement promoted the authority of the **Vedas** (with the slogan **'Go Back to the Vedas'**) and rejected **priesthood** and **idol worship**.

questions.question: According to Article 39A, the State shall:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**provide free legal aid**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 39A** was inserted into the **Constitution of India** by the **42nd Amendment Act, 1976**, to ensure that the legal system promotes justice on the basis of **equal opportunity**.
 
• The article mandates that the **State** shall provide **free legal aid** through suitable legislation or schemes to ensure that opportunities for securing justice are not denied to any citizen by reason of **economic or other disabilities**.
 
• It is categorized under the **Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP)** in **Part IV**, which serves as a constitutional guide for the government to establish social and economic democracy.
 
• The provision emphasizes that the **judiciary** and the **legal system** must be accessible to the marginalized sections of society, reinforcing the concept of **Equal Justice**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Legal Services Authorities Act, 1987**:

 
 
• This act was passed to give a statutory base to the **legal aid** programs and to provide free and competent legal services to the weaker sections.
 
• It led to the constitution of the **National Legal Services Authority (NALSA)** at the national level and **State Legal Services Authorities** at the state levels.
 
 
 
• **Other Articles mentioned in options**:
 
 
• **Religious Freedom**: Guaranteed under **Articles 25 to 28** of the Constitution as **Fundamental Rights** in **Part III**.
 
• **Clean Drinking Water**: Often interpreted as a part of the **Right to Life** under **Article 21** and the State duty to improve public health under **Article 47**.
 
• **International Peace and Security**: Explicitly mentioned under **Article 51**, which directs the State to maintain just and honorable relations between nations.

questions.question: The Confederation of Indian Industry (CII) successfully concluded the 13th edition of EXCON 2025 in which of the following cities?

questions.question: In which year did the Government of India declare Odia as a classical language?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**2014**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Union Cabinet** of India officially approved the classification of **Odia** as a **Classical Language** on **February 20, 2014**.
 
• It became the **sixth** language in India to be accorded this status, following the recommendations of a committee of experts constituted by the **Ministry of Culture**.
 
• **Odia** is the first language from the **Indo-Aryan** group to be recognized as classical, primarily because its literary tradition is distinct and has existed for over **1,500 to 2,000 years**.
 
• The criteria for this status involve high antiquity of early texts, a body of ancient literature considered a heritage by generations, and a literary tradition that is original and not borrowed from another speech community.
 
• The declaration followed a long-standing demand by the state government of **Odisha** and various linguistic experts who provided evidence of the language's ancient roots, such as the **Kalinga** inscriptions and the **Mahabharata** by **Sarala Das**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Government of India has recognized several other languages as classical over the years:
 
 
• **Tamil**: The first language to be designated as classical in **2004**.
 
• **Sanskrit**: Awarded the status in **2005** due to its vast and ancient religious and philosophical texts.
 
• **Kannada** and **Telugu**: Both were officially recognized in the year **2008**.
 
• **Malayalam**: Designated as a classical language in **2013**.
 
 
 
• Benefits of Classical Status:
 
 
• Establishment of a **Centre of Excellence for Studies in Classical Languages** to promote research and preservation.
 
• The **University Grants Commission** (UGC) creates professional chairs for these languages in **Central Universities**.
 
• Two major international awards are presented annually to scholars of eminence who have made significant contributions to the language.

questions.question: Which one of the following is NOT true in regard to The Waqf (Amendment) Bill, 2025 passed by the Indian government?

options.text: The bill also seeks to improve the economic and social status of Muslim women.
The bill retains two Muslim women members in central Waqf council.
The bill retains two Muslim women members in state Waqf board.
Female heirs are not guaranteed their rightful share in family waqf.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Female heirs are not guaranteed their rightful share in family waqf.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Waqf (Amendment) Bill, 2024** (referred to as 2025 in legislative context) explicitly aims to reform the management of waqf assets to improve the **social and economic status** of **Muslim women** by providing them with greater roles in administration and safeguarding their rights. ***Hence, statement 1 is correct.***
 
• One of the primary structural changes proposed in the Bill is the mandatory inclusion of **two Muslim women** as members of the **Central Waqf Council**, ensuring gender representation at the national level. ***Hence, statement 2 is correct.***
 
• The Bill also mandates that every **State Waqf Board** must have **two Muslim women** members, thereby institutionalizing women’s participation in the governance of waqf properties at the state level. ***Hence, statement 3 is correct.***
 
• In a significant legal shift regarding **Waqf-alal-aulad** (family waqf), the Bill introduces a proviso stating that the creation of a family waqf must not result in the denial of **inheritance rights** to any heir, including **female heirs**. This means the Bill **guarantees** their rightful share rather than denying it. ***Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Waqf-alal-aulad:**

 
 
• It refers to a **Waqf** created for the maintenance and support of the **waqif’s** (dedicator’s) own family, children, and descendants.
 
• Historically, there were concerns that such endowments were used to bypass the standard **Islamic Law of Inheritance**, often at the expense of women; the new amendment explicitly addresses this loophole.
 
 
 
• **Governance Reforms:**
 
 
• The Bill seeks to replace the **Waqf Act, 1995**, and introduces the **District Collector** as the primary authority to determine whether a property is **Waqf property** or government land.
 
• It also proposes the establishment of a separate **Board of Auqaf** for **Bohras** and **Aghakhanis** to ensure specialized representation for these communities.
 
• The Bill was referred to a **Joint Parliamentary Committee (JPC)** in **August 2024** for detailed scrutiny following debates in the **Lok Sabha**.

questions.question: भारत में निम्नलिखित में से कौन-सा क्षेत्र, स्थानीय रूप से प्लाया (playas) के नाम से जानी जाने वाली खारी झीलों से पहचाना जाता है?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**थार मरुस्थल**__.

__
 
• **थार मरुस्थल**, जिसे **महान भारतीय मरुस्थल** भी कहा जाता है, मुख्य रूप से **राजस्थान** में स्थित है और यहाँ कई शुष्क बेसिन पाए जाते हैं जिन्हें स्थानीय रूप से **प्लाया** (Playas) कहा जाता है।
 
• ये **लवणीय झीलें** (Salt Lakes) मरुस्थल के भीतर **अंतःस्थलीय अपवाह** (Inland Drainage) प्रणाली का परिणाम हैं, जहाँ नदियाँ समुद्र तक पहुँचने के बजाय रेतीले धरातल या बेसिन में ही समाप्त हो जाती हैं।
 
• वाष्पीकरण की तीव्र दर और वर्षा की कमी के कारण, इन बेसिनों के तल पर **सोडियम क्लोराइड** और अन्य खनिजों की मोटी परतें जमा हो जाती हैं, जिससे ये झीलों का जल **अत्यधिक खारा** हो जाता है।
 
• राजस्थान में स्थित **सांभर झील**, **डिडवाना**, **पंचपदरा**, **कुचामन** और **लूनकरणसर** झीलों को भौगोलिक रूप से प्लाया की श्रेणी में रखा जाता है।
 
• वैज्ञानिक दृष्टिकोण से, इन क्षेत्रों को **टेथिस सागर** के अवशेषों के रूप में देखा जाता है, जो इस क्षेत्र की मिट्टी में लवण की उच्च सांद्रता का मुख्य कारण है।

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **मालाबार तट**:

 
 
• यह भारत के दक्षिण-पश्चिमी तट (मुख्यतः **केरल**) पर स्थित है।
 
• यह क्षेत्र अपने लैगून और बैकवाटर्स के लिए प्रसिद्ध है, जिन्हें स्थानीय भाषा में **कयाल** (Kayals) कहा जाता है, न कि प्लाया।
 
 
 
• **दक्कन का पठार**:
 
 
• यह भारत का सबसे बड़ा पठार है, जो **क्रिटेशियस काल** के दौरान हुए **बेसाल्टिक लावा** के उद्गार से बना है।
 
• यहाँ की मिट्टी मुख्य रूप से **काली मिट्टी** (रेगुर) है, और यहाँ प्लाया जैसी मरुस्थलीय स्थलाकृतियाँ नहीं पाई जाती हैं।
 
 
 
• **पश्चिमी घाट**:
 
 
• इसे **सह्याद्रि** के नाम से भी जाना जाता है और यह भारत के प्रमुख **जैव विविधता हॉटस्पॉट** में से एक है।
 
• यह एक निरंतर पर्वत श्रृंखला है जहाँ भारी **मानसूनी वर्षा** होती है, जो शुष्क प्लाया झीलों के निर्माण के विपरीत स्थितियाँ प्रदान करती है।

questions.question: Which Amendment added Konkani, Manipuri, and Nepali to the Eighth Schedule?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**71st Amendment**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **71st Amendment Act** was enacted in **1992** to amend the **Eighth Schedule** of the **Constitution of India**.
 
• This amendment officially included three regional languages: **Konkani**, **Manipuri**, and **Nepali** into the list of scheduled languages.
 
• Prior to this amendment, the **Eighth Schedule** contained **15 languages**; the addition of these three languages increased the total count to **18**.
 
• The **Eighth Schedule** provides a list of languages that enjoy official status and constitutional recognition, influencing the composition of the **Official Languages Commission**.
 
• Including a language in this schedule entitles it to various forms of state support for its promotion and development across the **Indian Union**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **63rd Amendment Act, 1989**:

 
 
• This amendment repealed the **59th Amendment Act**, which had empowered the government to impose **Emergency** in **Punjab** based on internal disturbances.
 
 
 
• **52ⁿd Amendment Act, 1985**:
 
 
• Commonly referred to as the **Anti-Defection Law**, it inserted the **Tenth Schedule** to prevent elected members from switching political parties after elections.
 
 
 
• **42ⁿd Amendment Act, 1976**:
 
 
• Often called the **Mini-Constitution**, it brought massive changes including the addition of **Socialist**, **Secular**, and **Integrity** to the **Preamble** and established **Fundamental Duties**.
 
 
 
• **Language Evolution in Eighth Schedule**:
 
 
• The schedule initially had **14 languages**. **Sindhi** was added by the **21st Amendment** in **1967**.
 
• Later, the **92ⁿd Amendment** in **2003** added **Bodo**, **Dogri**, **Maithili**, and **Santhali**, bringing the current total to **22 languages**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **1857 के विद्रोह** ने ब्रिटिश राज को यह अहसास कराया कि भारतीय सैनिकों की एकता उनके साम्राज्य के लिए सबसे बड़ा खतरा है। इसलिए, विद्रोह के बाद सैन्य पुनर्गठन का प्राथमिक उद्देश्य भविष्य में किसी भी **एकीकृत सैन्य विद्रोह** की संभावना को पूरी तरह समाप्त करना था।
 
• सैन्य सुधारों के लिए 1858 में **पील कमीशन (Peel Commission)** का गठन किया गया था। इसकी सिफारिशों के आधार पर, सेना में ब्रिटिश और भारतीय सैनिकों के अनुपात में बदलाव किया गया ताकि नियंत्रण मजबूत रहे।

questions.question: Western Scholar Pishel associated the terms *Sutradhar* and *Sthapak* in Sanskrit plays with:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Puppet dance tradition**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Richard Pischel**, a distinguished **German Indologist**, was a primary advocate of the theory that **Sanskrit drama** originated from the **puppet theater** (known as **Puttalika** or **Puttika-nritya**) of ancient India.
 
• The term **Sutradhara**, which refers to the stage manager or director in **Classical Sanskrit plays**, literally translates to **'string-holder'** or **'thread-puller'** (from **Sutra** meaning thread and **Dhara** meaning holder). Pischel argued that this nomenclature is a direct vestige of the puppeteer who manipulated the strings of marionettes.
 
• The **Sthapak** (meaning 'the establisher' or 'the one who places') was a character who followed the **Sutradhara** in early dramatic traditions to introduce the play's prologue. Pischel linked this role to the assistant who physically arranged the puppets on the stage before the narrative began.
 
• Pischel detailed his findings in his influential work **'Die Heimat des Puppenspiels'** (The Home of the Puppet Play, 1900), where he contended that **shadow plays** and **puppet shows** provided the technical and structural foundation for human actors to later adopt.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Richard Pischel** (1849–1908):

 
 
• He was a leading specialist in **Prakrit** languages and **Buddhist studies**.
 
• His research suggested that India was the original home of puppet theater, which eventually spread to other parts of **Asia** and the **Middle East**.
 
 
 
• **Sanskrit Drama Roles**:
 
 
• **Sutradhara**: Responsible for performing the **Purvaranga** (preliminaries) and the **Nandi** (benedictory prayer). He essentially 'holds the thread' of the entire performance.
 
• **Classical Dance Performances**: While related to the **Natyashastra**, these are primarily based on **Abhinaya** (expression) and **Nritya** (dance), whereas Pischel specifically focused on the mechanical etymology of **Sutradhara**.
 
• **Ancient Musical Instruments** and **Ritual Ceremonies**: Other scholars, like **Sylvain Levi** and **Hillebrandt**, proposed that drama originated from **Vedic rituals** and **religious festivals**, but they did not utilize the **Sutradhara-Puppet** etymological link as Pischel did.

questions.question: Which information is essential to perform stoichiometric calculations for a chemical reaction?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**A balanced chemical equation**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Stoichiometry** is a section of chemistry that involves calculating the **quantitative relationships** or ratios between **reactants** and **products** in a chemical reaction.
 
• The fundamental basis for all stoichiometric calculations is a **balanced chemical equation**, which serves as a mathematical statement of the **Law of Conservation of Mass**.
 
• In a balanced equation, the **stoichiometric coefficients** (the numbers in front of the chemical formulas) represent the **mole ratios** of the substances; for example, in the reaction 2H₂ + O₂ → 2H₂O, the ratio of hydrogen to oxygen is 2:1.
 
• These **molar ratios** are essential for converting between **mass**, **moles**, and **particles** (atoms or molecules) using **Avogadro’s number** (6.022 × 10²³) and **molar mass**.
 
• Without a balanced equation, it is impossible to determine how much of one reactant is needed to react completely with another or to predict the **theoretical yield** of a product.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Variables in Chemical Reactions**:

 
 
• **Temperature and Pressure**: While these are vital for determining the **volume of gases** using the **Ideal Gas Law** (PV = nRT) or influencing **reaction rates** (kinetics), they do not provide the fundamental ratio of atoms required for stoichiometry.
 
• **Physical Attributes**: Factors like the **color of reactants** or the **type of apparatus** (flasks, beakers, or calorimeters) used are experimental details and have no impact on the mathematical stoichiometry of the reaction.
 
• **Limiting Reagents**: Stoichiometry is also used to identify the **limiting reactant**, which is the reactant that is completely consumed first, thereby limiting the amount of product formed.
 
 

Therefore, a balanced chemical equation is the correct answer

questions.question: Which quantities influence the kinetic energy of a moving body?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Both mass and velocity**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Kinetic Energy (K.E.)** is the energy possessed by an object due to its **motion**. It represents the amount of work required to accelerate an object of a specific **mass** from a state of rest to its current **velocity**.
 
• The mathematical formula for calculating kinetic energy is **K.E. = 1/2 × m × v²**. In this equation, **m** denotes the **mass** of the body and **v** represents its **velocity** or speed.
 
• The influence of **mass** is linear; if the mass of a moving object is doubled while keeping its speed constant, its kinetic energy will exactly **double**.
 
• The influence of **velocity** is exponential; because the velocity term is **squared** in the formula, doubling the speed of an object results in a **fourfold** increase in its kinetic energy.
 
• Since both variables appear in the numerator of the energy equation, it is established that the total energy of motion depends simultaneously on how much **matter** is moving and how **fast** it is traveling.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Scalar Property**:

 
 
• Kinetic energy is a **scalar quantity**, meaning it has magnitude but no specific direction. Even if the direction of velocity changes, the energy remains the same as long as the **speed** and **mass** are constant.
 
 
 
• **SI Unit**:
 
 
• The standard unit for measuring kinetic energy is the **Joule (J)**. One Joule is defined as **1 kg·m²/s²**.
 
 
 
• **Incorrect Factor Breakdown**:
 
 
• **Shape**: The physical **geometric shape** of an object does not determine its translational kinetic energy, though it can influence **air resistance** or **rotational inertia** in specific dynamics.
 
• **Only Velocity/Mass**: These options are incomplete because kinetic energy cannot exist without both an **inertial component** (mass) and a **dynamic component** (velocity).

questions.question: Who is credited with codifying the method of Carnatic music?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Purandara Dasa**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Purandara Dasa** (1484−1564) is universally revered as the **Sangeeta Pitamaha** (the Grandfather of Carnatic Music) for his monumental work in systematizing the foundation of the South Indian classical music tradition.
 
• He is credited with creating a structured **pedagogical curriculum** that is still strictly followed by students today, which includes graded exercises such as **Sarali Varisai**, **Janti Varisai**, **Dhatu Varisai**, and **Alankaras**.
 
• He introduced the **Mayamalavagowla** raga as the standard foundational scale for beginners, replacing the older practice of using **Kharaharapriya**, due to its symmetrical intervals which aid in voice stabilization.
 
• He formalized the **Suladi Sapta Tala** system, which consists of seven basic rhythmic cycles that serve as the rhythmic cornerstone for thousands of Carnatic compositions.
 
• His vast body of work includes thousands of **Devarnamas** and **Kirtanas** composed in the **Kannada** language, which successfully integrated complex musical structures with the **Bhakti** movement's philosophy.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

• His famous works include **Nala Charitre**, **Haribhakti Sara**, and **Ramadhanya Charitre**.
 
 
 
• **Jagannatha Dasa**:
 
 
• An 18th-century scholar and saint of the **Haridasa** lineage, best known for the philosophical treatise **Harikathamritasara**.
 
• He contributed significantly to the spread of **Madhva** philosophy through lyrical **Dasa Sahitya**.
 
 
 
• **Gopala Dasa**:
 
 
• An influential 18th-century poet-saint from **Karnataka** who is regarded as the disciple of **Vijaya Dasa**.
 
• He was instrumental in the spiritual initiation of Jagannatha Dasa and is celebrated for his deep mystical insights in his **Suladis**.

questions.question: Who among the following appoints judges of Family Courts in India?

• The appointment of judges to the **Family Courts** in India is governed by the statutory provisions of the **Family Courts Act, 1984**, which was enacted to promote conciliation and speedy settlement of matrimonial disputes.
 
• According to **Section 4** of the **Family Courts Act, 1984**, the **State Government** is the competent authority empowered to appoint one or more persons as judges of the Family Court.
 
• The **State Government** must exercise this power only with the **concurrence of the High Court** of the respective state to ensure judicial independence and merit.
 
• The Act specifies that the **State Government** should provide preference to **women** in the appointment of judges to ensure a more sensitive approach to family matters, as mentioned under **Section 4(4)**.

• Under **Article 233** of the **Indian Constitution**, the **Governor** appoints **District Judges** in consultation with the **High Court**. While the Governor handles regular judicial service appointments, the specific statutory power for Family Court judges is vested in the **State Government**.

questions.question: How many Fundamental Duties were finally included in the Constitution in 1976 (based on committee recommendations)?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ten**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Fundamental Duties** of citizens were not part of the original **Constitution of India** that came into force in **1950**.
 
• They were incorporated into the Constitution via the **42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976**, during the period of **National Emergency**.
 
• The amendment followed the recommendations of the **Sardar Swaran Singh Committee**, which was tasked with suggesting duties that citizens should perform in exchange for their rights.
 
• While the **Swaran Singh Committee** originally suggested the inclusion of **eight** duties, the Union Government decided to include a total of **ten** Fundamental Duties at the time of the amendment.
 
• These duties were consolidated into a new **Part IV-A** of the Constitution, specifically under **Article 51A**.
 
• The list included duties such as abiding by the Constitution, **cherishing the noble ideals** of the national struggle for freedom, and **safeguarding public property**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **86th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2002**:

 
 
• The total count of Fundamental Duties increased from **ten to eleven** through this amendment.
 
• It added the duty of a parent or guardian to provide **opportunities for education** to their child or ward between the age of **6 and 14 years**.
 
 
 
• **Source and Nature**:
 
 
• The idea of Fundamental Duties was inspired by the Constitution of the **USSR** (Union of Soviet Socialist Republics).
 
• Unlike Fundamental Rights, these duties are **non-justiciable**, meaning citizens cannot be punished by the courts for not following them unless a specific **Parliamentary law** (like the Prevention of Insults to National Honour Act) is enacted for that purpose.
 
 
 
• **Verma Committee (1999)**:
 
 
• This committee identified the existence of **legal provisions** for the implementation of some of the Fundamental Duties, emphasizing that the **state** can enforce them through legislative action.

questions.question: In Windows 11, what is the purpose of using dir /s /b "syllabus.pdf" inside Command Prompt?

options.text: To copy “syllabus.pdf” into a new destination folder
To list full file paths of “syllabus.pdf” from all nested folders
To show the file size and attributes of “report.pdf”
To open “syllabus.pdf” using the default PDF viewer

questions.solution:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **dir command** is a fundamental **Command Line Interface (CLI)** utility in **Windows 11** used to list the contents of a directory, including files and subfolders.
 
• The **/s switch** is a recursive parameter that instructs the **Command Prompt** to search not only the current directory but also every **nested subdirectory** within the specified path.
 
• The **/b switch** activates the **bare format**, which strips away metadata such as file size, timestamps, and the summary footer, leaving only the names of the files.
 
• When **/s** and **/b** are combined, the output behavior changes to display the **fully qualified path** (the absolute location starting from the drive letter) for every matching file found in the hierarchy.
 
• By specifying the filename **‘syllabus.pdf’**, the command acts as a precise **search tool** that scans the entire drive or folder tree to find every instance of that specific document and reports its exact location.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Comparison with other **Windows commands**:

 
 
• **copy command**: This is used to replicate a file from a **source** to a **destination**. It does not simply list paths; it performs a data transfer operation.
 
• **start command**: This utility is used to execute a file. For a **PDF**, it would trigger the **default PDF viewer** (like Microsoft Edge or Adobe Acrobat) to open the file.
 
• **attrib command**: This command is used to display or change **file attributes**, such as Read-only (R), Archive (A), System (S), and Hidden (H), rather than just searching for filenames.
 
 
 
• Advanced usage of **dir**:
 
 
• **Wildcards**: Users can search for all files of a specific type by using an **asterisk (*)**, such as **dir /s /b *.pdf** to list every PDF on the system.
 
• **Output Redirection**: The results of this search can be saved to a text file by appending **> results.txt** to the end of the command.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is true for water when it is cooled from 4°C to 0°C?

options.text: Volume decreases but density remains same

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Volume increases but density decreases**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Water exhibits a unique physical phenomenon known as **Anomalous Expansion** when cooled or heated within the specific temperature range of **0°C to 4°C**.
 
• Under normal conditions, most liquids contract upon cooling; however, water reaches its **maximum density** (1 g/cm³ or 1000 kg/m³) and **minimum volume** precisely at **4°C**.
 
• As water is cooled from **4°C down to 0°C**, the **hydrogen bonds** between water molecules begin to arrange themselves into a rigid, open-cage **hexagonal crystalline structure**.
 
• This molecular orientation causes the molecules to push further apart compared to their state at 4°C, which results in a measurable **increase in volume**.
 
• Since **Density** is defined as mass per unit volume, and the mass of the water remains constant, the **increase in volume** leads to a corresponding **decrease in density** as the temperature approaches the freezing point.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Ecological Significance:**

 
 
• The decrease in density as water nears **0°C** ensures that **ice floats** on the surface of lakes and ponds.
 
• This floating ice layer acts as a **thermal insulator**, maintaining the liquid water below at **4°C**, which is vital for the survival of **aquatic life** during extreme winters.
 
 
 
• **Physical Impact:**
 
 
• When water freezes into **ice** at 0°C, its volume expands by approximately **9%**.
 
• This expansion generates immense pressure, often leading to the **weathering of rocks** in geology or the **bursting of water pipes** in cold climates.

questions.question: Khut, Muqaddam and Patwari during the Delhi Sultanate were _________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**village functionaries**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **village** (referred to as **Deh** or **Mauza**) was the smallest unit of administration during the **Delhi Sultanate**, and its management relied on local traditional authorities.
 
• **Khuts** and **Muqaddams** were hereditary village headmen or rural aristocrats who acted as intermediaries between the state and the peasantry for the collection of land revenue.
 
• The **Muqaddam** was primarily responsible for maintaining law and order within the village and ensuring that the designated taxes were collected from the cultivators.
 
• The **Patwari** served as the village accountant whose primary duty was to maintain meticulous records of land holdings, crop production, and the **Kharaj** (land tax) owed by the peasants.
 
• During the reign of **Sultan Alauddin Khalji**, the privileges of these village functionaries were strictly curtailed, and they were forced to pay taxes like ordinary peasants to prevent them from becoming too powerful or wealthy at the expense of the state treasury.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Administrative Hierarchy**:

 
 
• **Iqta (Province)**: Managed by **Muqtis** or **Walis**, who were high-ranking **provincial functionaries** responsible for law, order, and military supply.
 
• **Shiq (District)**: Governed by a **Shiqdar**, who oversaw the administration of several parganas.
 
• **Pargana (Group of Villages)**: The unit between the Shiq and the village, headed by an **Amil** (revenue officer) and a **Mushrif** (accountant).
 
• **Town Administration**: Managed by the **Kotwal**, who was the chief **town functionary** responsible for municipal duties and policing.
 
 
 
• **Revenue System**: The Sultanate primarily relied on land revenue, and officials like the **Mushrif-i-Mamalik** (Accountant General) at the center oversaw the overall financial health of the empire, while the local **village functionaries** ensured grassroots implementation.

questions.question: DNA and RNA are polymers made of long chains of ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Nucleotides**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA)** and **ribonucleic acid (RNA)** are essential biological macromolecules found in all living organisms.
 
• These structures are biopolymers composed of repeating monomeric units called **nucleotides**.
 
• Each individual nucleotide is chemically structured with three primary components: a **pentose sugar** (deoxyribose in DNA and ribose in RNA), a **phosphate group**, and a nitrogen-containing **nitrogenous base**.
 
• The nucleotides are covalently joined together by **phosphodiester bonds**, which form between the phosphate group of one nucleotide and the sugar of the next, creating a stable sugar-phosphate backbone.
 
• DNA contains the nitrogenous bases **adenine (A)**, **guanine (G)**, **cytosine (C)**, and **thymine (T)**, whereas RNA replaces thymine with **uracil (U)**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Monosaccharides**:

 
 
• These are the simplest units of **carbohydrates** (simple sugars) like glucose and fructose.
 
• They serve as the building blocks for complex polysaccharides such as **cellulose**, **starch**, and **glycogen**.
 
 
 
• **Fatty acids**:
 
 
• These consist of a carboxylic acid with a long aliphatic chain.
 
• They are the fundamental components of **lipids**, which play a crucial role in forming **cell membranes** (phospholipids) and storing energy (triglycerides).
 
 
 
• **Amino acids**:
 
 
• These are organic molecules consisting of a basic amino group, an acidic carboxyl group, and an organic R group.
 
• They are the monomers that polymerize via **peptide bonds** to form **proteins**, which carry out cellular structure and enzymatic functions.

questions.question: Which wildlife conservation strategy protects entire ecosystems rather than a single species?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**In-situ conservation**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **In-situ conservation** is the strategy of protecting a **species** in its **natural habitat**. Instead of focusing on a single organism, this method aims to preserve the **entire ecosystem** and the complex interactions between various species.
 
• By safeguarding the **natural environment**, all organisms within that ecosystem—including **plants**, **animals**, and **microbes**—are protected simultaneously, ensuring the maintenance of **ecological processes**.
 
• This strategy is often described as **on-site conservation**. It is the most effective way to maintain **genetic diversity** and allow for the ongoing **evolution** of species within their native ranges.
 
• Common examples of this strategy include the establishment of **National Parks**, **Wildlife Sanctuaries**, **Biosphere Reserves**, and **Sacred Groves**.
 
• In the context of **India**, there are currently **18 Biosphere Reserves**, over **100 National Parks**, and more than **500 Wildlife Sanctuaries** dedicated to this holistic protection approach.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Ex-situ Conservation**: This involves the protection of components of **biological diversity** outside their natural habitats.

 
 
• **Seed Banks**: These are facilities where **seeds** are stored at very low temperatures to preserve **genetic variety** for the long term. This is a species-specific or crop-specific approach.
 
• **Captive Breeding**: This refers to the process of **breeding animals** in controlled environments like **zoos** or specialized facilities to increase population numbers of **endangered species**.
 
 
 
• **Biodiversity Hotspots**:
 
 
• These are specific **geographical regions** that host extremely high levels of **species richness** and **endemism** (species found nowhere else).
 
• To qualify as a hotspot, a region must contain at least **1,500 species of vascular plants** as endemics and have lost at least **70 percent** of its original native vegetation.
 
• There are currently **36 biodiversity hotspots** globally, which are prioritized for **in-situ conservation** efforts.

questions.question: In Windows 11 operating system, what happens when Alt + F4 is pressed while no applications or windows are open?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Shows the system shutdown dialog**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In the **Windows 11** operating system, the **Alt + F4** keyboard shortcut is primarily designed to close the active application window currently in focus.
 
• When no applications are open, or when the user has clicked on the **Desktop** (making it the active interface), pressing **Alt + F4** triggers the **Shut Down Windows** dialog box.
 
• The resulting dialog box provides a drop-down menu with various power management options, including **Shut down**, **Restart**, **Sleep**, **Hibernate**, and **Sign out**.
 
• This functionality is a legacy feature of the **Windows Graphical User Interface (GUI)** that allows users to quickly power off the system without navigating through the **Start Menu**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Task Manager**:

 
 
• The primary shortcut to open the **Task Manager** is **Ctrl + Shift + Esc**.
 
• It is used to monitor **system performance**, manage **startup apps**, and terminate unresponsive **background processes**.
 
 
 
• **File Explorer**:
 
 
• The standard keyboard shortcut to launch **File Explorer** in Windows is **Windows Key + E**.
 
• It serves as the main **file management** application for accessing **folders**, **drives**, and **network locations**.
 
 
 
• **Refresh Function**:
 
 
• The **F5** key or **Ctrl + R** is typically used to refresh the active window or the **Desktop environment**.
 
• Refreshing updates the display to reflect recent changes in **file metadata** or **icon arrangements**.

questions.question: What is the maximum loan amount available under PMMY for entrepreneurs who have successfully repaid previous ‘Tarun’ category loans?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**₹20 lakh**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Pradhan Mantri Mudra Yojana (PMMY)** is a flagship scheme of the **Government of India** launched on **April 8, 2015**, to provide collateral-free institutional credit to **small/micro-enterprises**.
 
• In the **Union Budget 2024-25**, the Finance Minister announced a significant enhancement to the loan limits under the scheme to support maturing businesses.
 
• The loan limit for the **Tarun** category was increased from the previous maximum of **₹10 lakh** to **₹20 lakh**.
 
• This enhanced limit of **₹20 lakh** is specifically available for those entrepreneurs who have **successfully repaid** their previous loans under the **Tarun** category, demonstrating high creditworthiness.
 
• This move aims to provide larger financial buffers to small business owners, enabling them to scale up their operations and transition into larger industrial or service units.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **PMMY** classifies loans into three distinct categories based on the stage of growth and funding requirements of the micro-unit:

 
 
• **Shishu**: Covers loans up to **₹50,000**, intended for entrepreneurs who are either in their first stage of business or require very small capital.
 
• **Kishore**: Covers loans above **₹50,000** and up to **₹5 lakh**, targeting units that have already started and need funds for expansion.
 
• **Tarun**: Originally covered loans above **₹5 lakh** and up to **₹10 lakh**, representing the highest tier for established enterprises.
 
 
 
• **MUDRA** stands for **Micro Units Development & Refinance Agency Ltd.**, which acts as a refinancing body for **Public Sector Banks**, **Regional Rural Banks (RRBs)**, and **Non-Banking Financial Companies (NBFCs)**.
 
• The scheme focuses on the **Non-Corporate Small Business Sector (NCSB)**, which includes small manufacturing units, service sector units, and shopkeepers.

questions.question: Which Article prohibits judicial inquiry into ministerial advice tendered to President during constitutional functioning?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 74**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 74(1)** of the **Indian Constitution** provides for a **Council of Ministers** with the **Prime Minister** at the head to **aid and advise** the **President**, who shall, in the exercise of his functions, act in accordance with such advice.
 
• **Article 74(2)** explicitly states that the question of whether any, and if so what, **advice was tendered** by Ministers to the **President** shall not be **inquired into in any court**.
 
• This provision serves to protect the **confidentiality** of the **deliberations** between the **President** and the **Council of Ministers**, ensuring the **executive branch** can function without **judicial interference** in its internal advisory process.
 
• The **42nd Constitutional Amendment Act of 1976** made the advice of the **Council of Ministers** binding on the **President**, while the **44th Constitutional Amendment Act of 1978** allowed the **President** to require the Council to **reconsider** such advice once.
 
• In the landmark **S.R. Bommai v. Union of India (1994)** case, the **Supreme Court** clarified that while the **advice** itself is immune from **judicial inquiry**, the **material** on which the advice is based is subject to **judicial review**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Article 78**:

 
 
• It defines the **duties of the Prime Minister** as a **bridge** between the **Council of Ministers** and the **President**.
 
• The **Prime Minister** must communicate all **administrative decisions** and **proposals for legislation** to the **President**.
 
 
 
• **Article 72**:
 
 
• This article empowers the **President** to grant **pardons, reprieves, respites, or remissions** of punishment.
 
• It allows for the **suspension, remission, or commutation** of sentences in cases involving **Court Martials**, **death sentences**, or offenses against **Union laws**.
 
 
 
• **Article 76**:
 
 
• It provides for the **Attorney-General for India**, who is appointed by the **President** and holds office during their **pleasure**.
 
• The **Attorney-General** is the **chief legal advisor** to the **Government of India** and has the **right of audience** in all courts within **India**.

questions.question: Which one of the following represents the correct formula for crude birth rate (CBR), where B = live births during the year; P= Estimated mid year population of the area?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**(Births div Population) times 1000**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Crude Birth Rate (CBR)** is a primary demographic indicator used to quantify the frequency of **live births** within a specific population over a defined period, typically one calendar year.
 
• The numerator **B** represents the total number of **live births** recorded in a specific geographical area during the year, excluding stillbirths or other non-live deliveries.
 
• The denominator **P** represents the **estimated mid-year population** of that area, which serves as the conventional standard to account for population changes occurring throughout the year.
 
• The ratio of births to population is multiplied by a constant factor of **1,000** to express the rate as the number of births per thousand inhabitants, facilitating easier cross-regional comparisons.
 
• It is designated as **crude** because it considers the total population as the denominator, without adjusting for **age-specific** or **sex-specific** structures, such as the proportion of women in **reproductive age groups**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Demographic Metrics**:

 
 
• **Crude Death Rate (CDR)**: Calculated using a similar methodology, where the number of deaths in a year is divided by the **mid-year population** and multiplied by **1,000**.
 
• **Rate of Natural Increase**: Derived by subtracting the **Crude Death Rate** from the **Crude Birth Rate** (CBR − CDR), representing population growth excluding **migration** effects.
 
• **General Fertility Rate (GFR)**: A more refined measure than CBR, as it relates the number of births specifically to the number of **women of childbearing age** (usually 15−49 years).
 
• **Total Fertility Rate (TFR)**: The average number of children a woman would have if she survived to the end of her **reproductive years** and bore children according to current age-specific fertility rates.
 
 
 
• **Socio-Economic Importance**:
 
 
• High **Crude Birth Rates** are typically observed in developing nations with limited access to **family planning** and lower levels of female **literacy**.
 
• Data regarding CBR is vital for **urban planning**, forecasting **educational infrastructure** needs, and formulating **public health policies**.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a pull factor of migration?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Socio-economic backwardness**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Migration is generally influenced by two sets of factors: **Push factors** and **Pull factors**.
 
• **Pull factors** are positive conditions at a destination that attract people to move there. They include factors like **better job opportunities**, **higher wages**, **peace and stability**, **security of life**, and **pleasant climate**.
 
• **Push factors** are negative conditions at the place of origin that compel or force people to leave. Examples include **unemployment**, **poverty**, **political turmoil**, **natural disasters**, and **socio-economic backwardness**.
 
• **Socio-economic backwardness** refers to a lack of development, poor educational infrastructure, inadequate healthcare, and low standards of living in a region. These conditions make a place less desirable to live in, thereby acting as a **Push factor** rather than a pull factor.
 
• **Better job opportunities** act as a magnet for migrants seeking economic advancement and are a primary **Pull factor** in urban and industrial centers.
 
• **Peace and stability** along with the **security of life** pull individuals away from regions affected by conflict, war, or high crime rates toward safer and more predictable environments.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Push Factors**:

 
 
• **Unemployment**: Lack of local livelihood options forces individuals to seek work elsewhere.
 
• **Political Turmoil**: Civil unrest, persecution, or unstable governments drive people out of their homelands.
 
• **Poor Living Conditions**: Includes lack of basic amenities like **clean water**, **electricity**, and **sanitation**.
 
 
 
• **Pull Factors**:
 
 
• **Economic Growth**: Regions with high **GDP growth** and industrialization attract labor.
 
• **Social Services**: Access to prestigious **educational institutions** and advanced **medical facilities** acts as a major pull for families.
 
• **Climatic Comfort**: Destinations with moderate or favorable weather conditions are often preferred by retirees and migrants.
